column2: On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest of faith.” Reported by Muslim.

Raʾā (“sees”): knows. Minkum (“among you”): you, the company of Muslims. Munkaran (“an evil”): something the Sharīʿah deems ugly and rejects. Fa-l-yughayyirhu (“let him change it”): let him remove it, bi-yadihi (“with his hand”): where it can be removed by hand. “If he cannot” oppose it with his hand, fa-bi-lisānihi (“then with his tongue”): by words. “And if he cannot” speak, fa-bi-qalbihi (“then with his heart”): he must oppose it [inwardly]. Aḍʿaf al-īmān (“the weakest of faith”): the least of it.
The obligation to change evil by every possible means: by hand, by tongue or by heart.
Whoever is able to do a quality of faith and does it is better than one who leaves it out of inability.
Evil should be changed only after verification, deliberation and certainty.
Not opposing [evil] even with the heart shows weakness of faith.
Whoever does not change an evil when it has been established and there is no obstacle is sinful for not removing it.
Changing evil has degrees, so each should change it only in the way he is able.

This hadith teaches us something of general benefit, beneficial to whoever carries it out and harmful to whoever does not act on it: every person who learns of an evil must remove it according to his ability. If he is strong enough for the highest level of removing evil, by hand, let him do so, whether literally or by the hand of someone else at his command.

Whoever is unable to do that, let him change it with his tongue, by forbidding the one committing it, making clear to him its harm and guiding him to good in place of this evil. If he is unable to do this level, let him change it with his heart, by hating this evil and the one who

does it, [resolving] that if he were able to remove it by hand or by tongue he would remove it. Changing by the heart is the weakest level of faith in changing evil, because its benefit does not extend beyond the person himself. None of these three levels is lifted from anyone together,
and there is no excuse for one who excuses himself from the least of them, which is opposing [evil] with the heart.
But it is as the poet said:
With salt is set right whatever is feared to spoil; / so what of the salt, if it is itself spoiled?
